transcript:
User: Hello — I got your flyer about after-hours calls. We miss calls when we're out on jobs.
Agent: Got it, thanks for calling — missing those calls while you’re out working is exactly what we focus on. When the phone rings and you’re on a job, what usually happens to that call — does it just go to voicemail, or is someone able to pick it up?
User: It usually goes to voicemail when we're out on jobs.
Agent: Mhm, I hear you — so most of those end up as voicemails. Do people actually leave messages and wait, or do you feel like a lot of them just call the next company if no one picks up?
User: About 8 calls a week go to voicemail, and I think about 50% would book if someone answered.
Agent: Got it — so roughly 8 a week, and half of those could’ve been bookings if someone picked up, that’s real money walking away. What kind of work do you do on those jobs — what industry are you in?
User: We're a home remodeling/contractor company in Denver, CO, handling various remodeling projects.
Agent: Makes sense, thanks for sharing — Denver remodeling, lots of project value in every call. When those 8 callers a week hit voicemail instead of a person, what do you think most of them do next — wait for you, or call another contractor right away?
User: I think about half of them would book if someone answered instead of reaching voicemail.
Agent: Yeah, that lines up with what we see — those missed calls are basically lost remodeling jobs. So… when you saw our flyer about after-hours calls, were you mainly hoping for a way to have those evening and “out on jobs” calls actually turn into booked estimates automatically?
User: Yes, exactly — we're looking to turn those missed calls into booked estimates automatically.
Agent: Got it, that makes total sense for a remodeling business. Mind if we do a quick 30-second calculation together on what those missed estimate calls are actually costing you each month?
User: Sure, let's do that calculation.
Agent: Great. So ballpark, what’s your average job or estimate value from those calls — are we talking more like $2,000, $5,000, $10,000 per project?
User: Our average job value is about $2,500 per project.
Agent: Right, so with 8 missed calls a week, 50% close rate, and $2,500 jobs, you’re leaking about $43,300 a month from calls that hit voicemail instead of booking. So… it’s a 20‑minute walkthrough where we plug in your numbers and show exactly how to turn those after-hours and “out on jobs” calls into booked estimates — what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works better for me.
Agent: Perfect, tomorrow’s great. First thing — what’s your first name?
User: I prefer to keep it professional. You can call me by the company name, 'Cornerstone Remodeling'.
Agent: Got it, Cornerstone Remodeling it is. And the number you’re calling from now — is this the best contact number for your confirmation text tomorrow?
User: Yes, my best contact number is +13039150001.
Agent: Mhm, perfect, I’ll use that for the confirmation text. And which time zone are you in — Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
Agent: So tomorrow’s good — I can get you in as soon as Wednesday at 10:30 or 11:15 in the morning, Mountain time; which works better for Cornerstone Remodeling?
User: We are in the Mountain timezone, which is America/Denver.
Agent: Got it, Mountain time in Denver, perfect. For the walkthrough, do you prefer Wednesday at 10:30 or 11:15 in the morning?
User: Wednesday at 10:30 in the morning works for me. Please go ahead and book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Cornerstone Remodeling, you’re all set — we’ve booked your 20-minute walkthrough with Jay for Wednesday at 10:30 in the morning, Denver time. You’ll get an SMS text with the confirmation details shortly — you can add it to your calendar in one tap or reschedule if something comes up. Is there anything else I can help you with before we wrap up?
